items.title: Ukraine reportedly targets Russian cruise missile fuel plant in Tver Oblast
items.summary: Ukraine's military launched an attack on Russia's Tver Oblast overnight on Oct. 9, reportedly targeting a Russian factory that manufactures fuel components for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, Russian Telegram media channels reported.

items.title: UK to provide $71 million winter aid package to Ukraine
items.summary: The latest announcement comes as Kyiv experienced widespread power outages on Oct. 8 following a Russian attack on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Over 3 million residents in the capital lost power in what officials described as "an attack on one of the energy facilities important for the city of Kyiv."

items.title: UK service member charged with spying for Russia makes first court appearance
items.summary: Under the U.K.'s National Security Act 2023, junior intelligence specialist Teddy Young, 24, was charged with two offenses for allegedly trying to pass protected information to a foreign power between November 2024 and May 2025.

items.title: Two trains collide in Lviv, injuring 8

items.title: Ukrainian investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach detained in Austria while on assignment

items.title: 'We always respond in kind' — Zelensky addresses Ukrainian attacks on Russian data center
items.summary: "We certainly are capable," Zelensky said about striking Russian data centers. "We always respond in kind. Regarding data centers, as you all know, they have been and still are striking our data centers."

items.title: Zelensky sends delegation to meet Trump envoys as he hints at secret US-Russia economic talks
items.summary: "Meetings are expected to take place over two days... we are counting on a European team to join our negotiating group," President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

items.title: Russia lifts quarantine in Irkutsk region, where lab worker allegedly died of plague

items.title: Open letter to the US administration: The G20 invitation to Putin should come with conditions

items.summary: The drop in voltage temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the Kyiv City State Administration (KMDA) said. Other parts of the capital's public transport network were also affected.

items.title: Moldova ready to take in more Ukrainian refugees come winter, Sandu says
items.summary: "If this winter in Ukraine is as difficult as the whole world expects, we are ready to receive as many people as need safety," Moldovan President Maia Sandu said at the Moldova Security Forum in Chisinau on Oct. 8.

items.title: South Korea to recall Ukraine envoy amid North Korean POWs dispute

items.title: Russian drone barrage on Kyiv kills 4, injures 19, disrupts electricity, water supplies

items.title: At least 33 dead after Russian glide bomb strikes Kramatorsk buses
items.summary: "Russia comes to the Ukrainian land with death," Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin said.

items.title: Department of War Awards $6.3 Billion Multi-Year Contract to RTX's Raytheon for SM-3 BLOCK IB Interceptors
items.summary: The War Department and the Missile Defense Agency awarded Raytheon, an RTX business, a multiyear procurement contract valued at up to $6.3 billion to produce Standard Missile–3 Block IB interceptors.

items.title: Department of War Announces $350 Million in Quantum Computing Initiatives
items.summary: The Office of the Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering announced new initiatives and programmatic updates totaling approximately $350 million to strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum computing capabilities that support national security.

items.title: Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital Signs $150 Million Conditional Loan Commitment With PsiQuantum

items.summary: Motivational incentives are known to improve working memory (WM) when items differ in value, but whether they enhance performance when all items are equally valued, and if so, by what mechanism, remains unclear. Improvements could reflect enhanced memory-based representations or speed-accuracy trade-offs, whereby incentives promote slower, more cautious responding without improving memory itself. items.summary: The balance between excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) neurons is fundamental to cortical function, and its disruption underlies a wide range of neurological disorders, including epilepsy, Alzheimers disease and autism spectrum disorder. Cortical organoids offer a promising model to study this balance, as they recapitulate key features of brain development, including the emergence of E/I circuitry. items.summary: Neural activity during performance of a cognitive or motor task is often described as lying on a low-dimensional manifold in the space of all possible activity patterns. When multiple tasks are performed, an individual brain region's activity may generate multiple such manifolds. Several models have been introduced to explain this capability, each with different assumptions concerning architecture and inputs. items.summary: Free recall of naturalistic stimuli, such as films and stories, reveals what people remember and how they organize it. Scoring such recall requires matching each recalled utterance to the encoded stimulus, and doing this manually often makes large studies impractical. Existing automated methods mostly return similarity or aggregate scores rather than explicit matches between recalled and stimulus content. items.title: Huntingtin and Celsr3 Orchestrate Spontaneous Long-Distance Spinal Cord Regeneration
items.summary: Spontaneous spinal cord regeneration is an endogenous process operational in diverse vertebrate and select mammalian species. Yet despite resulting in functional regeneration, axonal regrowth dynamics as well as underlying molecular programs are largely unknown. Live-cell imaging following laser axotomy of individual zebrafish spinal cord M-cell axons reveals a time-sensitive multistep process. items.title: Impaired value estimation over space explains turn-induced freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease: A cortico-basal ganglia-inspired reinforcement learning model
items.summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) gait is characterized by reduced walking speed, short shuffling steps, increased double stance time, and increased step time variability. The most debilitating symptom in PD is freezing of gait (FOG), a context-dependent locomotion arrest, mostly occurring while encountering turns, obstacles, and narrow pathways. FOG is more pronounced during turning, a complex task that challenges motor planning and execution. Here, we simulate this phenomenon using a computational model inspired by the cortico-basal ganglia circuitry, based on reinforcement learning (RL) principles.

These fiber populations include subcortical U-shaped fibers (U-fibers) that predominantly follow a tangential trajectory along the gray matter-white matter interface and long-range fibers that extend more radially through the deeper white matter to connect distant cortical regions. items.summary: Animals learn to select actions that maximize reward in complex environments. A central challenge in this process is credit routing: behavioral outcomes must be routed back to the neural populations that contributed to generating the relevant actions. One possible route is through thalamocortical pathways conveying learning signals from the basal ganglia and cerebellum, where plasticity is shaped by reward-prediction errors. items.summary: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), characterized by cerebrovascular amyloid deposition, is strongly associated with Alzheimers disease, ischemic injury, and lobar hemorrhages. APOE4 is the strongest known genetic risk factor for CAA, yet the cellular sources of APOE4 that drive pathogenic vascular amyloid deposition remain poorly defined. Here, we identify vascular-associated fibroblasts (VAFs) as a key source of APOE4 that mediates CAA and cerebrovascular dysfunction. items.summary: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), predominantly comprised of tau and TDP-43 proteinopathies, is a common cause of early-onset dementia. Biomarkers that reliably classify FTLD subtypes are limited, thereby hindering in-vivo diagnosis and clinical trial stratification. We conducted large-scale, multi-platform cerebrospinal fluid proteomics in 566 individuals, including 274 FTLD-spectrum (48 autopsy-confirmed FTLD-TDP, 90 autopsy-confirmed FTLD-tau), 171 Alzheimers disease, and 95 controls. items.summary: Neurodegenerative proteinopathies are defined by distinct proteins whose folding, trafficking and clearance depend on shared proteostasis machinery. items.summary: Although human perception appears continuous, converging evidence suggests that sensory input is integrated over discrete temporal windows. The duration of these Temporal Integration Windows (TIWs) determines the temporal resolution of perception, but how this fundamental property develops across infancy and childhood remains unknown. items.title: Widely Used Calculations of Intracranial Volume Provide Inaccurate Estimates in Developmental Cohorts: Evidence and Solutions for the Neuroimaging Community
items.summary: Intracranial volume (ICV) is often estimated as part of automated neuroimaging processing pipelines and commonly used to account for and characterize cranial size. FreeSurfer's estimated intracranial volume (eTIV) produces implausible longitudinal estimates in developmental samples when using versions prior to FreeSurfer 8. Across two different adolescent datasets, we document eTIV changes of up to 39% between 1.5 - 2 year sessions for FreeSurfer 7, with errors more pronounced on Siemens scanners and in female participants. items.title: Distilling Trial-Level EEG Variability into Participant Representations: Neurophysiologically Constrained Graph Learning in ADHD
items.summary: Extracting stable individual-level representations from noisy and variable trial-wise EEG remains a major challenge in computational cognitive neuroscience. We developed a spatiotemporal graph attention network to analyze Go/NoGo EEG from children and adolescents with and without ADHD. The framework combines ERP-informed temporal windows, phase-synchrony graph priors, and trial-to-participant transfer learning, making both information routing and representation geometry explicitly testable. items.title: Dynamic Modulation of Neural Cell Identity Maintenance via Lysine Acetyltransferase Type 3 Protein Targeted Degradation
items.summary: Cell identity acquisition during central nervous system development leads to the establishment of cell-specific transcriptional programs. Once acquired, this identity must be actively maintained, among other molecular mechanisms, by the acetylation of cell-type-specific regulatory regions carried out by the lysine acetyltransferases type 3 (KAT3) proteins CBP and p300.
